_about: Coaching staffs. Head coaches come from the schedule data automatically; edit this file when a coordinator or play caller changes. off_caller / def_caller: 'HC' if the head coach calls plays, otherwise 'OC' / 'DC'.
sources: Staffs and play callers: ran.de, 'Head Coaches, Coordinators, General Manager und Playcaller der Saison 2026' (updated Oct. 8, 2026). Scheme notes: ESPN NFL Nation, 'Who calls plays for every NFL team in 2026?' (Sept. 3, 2026). Defensive coordinators: Wikipedia, 'List of current NFL defensive coordinators'.
hc_ceo_note: Delegates play calling on both sides and runs the team as a CEO-style head coach.

BUF.off_scheme: Run-first on early downs built around Josh Allen: since Brady took over play calling in late 2023, Buffalo has called designed runs on 59% of first downs, the most in the NFL, and led the league in offensive EPA.
BUF.off_tree: Sean Payton (Saints offensive assistant); called plays in Carolina before Buffalo
BUF.off_philosophy: First-time head coach keeping the play sheet; added a dedicated run game coordinator this season.

MIA.off_scheme: Screen-heavy passing game (second-highest screen rate in 2025) built around running back De'Von Achane and the mobility of Malik Willis.
MIA.off_tree: Kyle Shanahan (49ers); former Texans offensive coordinator
MIA.off_philosophy: Tailors the offense to his personnel; Houston's top-10 passing offense in C.J. Stroud's rookie year was his.
MIA.def_scheme: Head coach Jeff Hafley calls the defense himself; a first-time NFL head coach who led Boston College for four seasons.

NE.off_scheme: Veteran system that pushed the ball downfield in 2025 (second-longest average pass distance), with Drake Maye taking more control at the line in year two.
NE.off_tree: Bill Belichick (Patriots), in his third stint as New England's coordinator
NE.off_philosophy: Game-plan specific; surrounded by former head coaches and coordinators on the offensive staff.
NE.def_scheme: First full year as coordinator after taking over defensive play calling during 2025.

NYJ.off_scheme: Leaning on the run game with more two-tight-end (12 personnel) looks than usual; historically sends five receivers into routes at a very high rate.
NYJ.off_philosophy: Main job is cutting down Geno Smith's interceptions in an offense that ranked 29th in scoring.
NYJ.def_scheme: Head coach Aaron Glenn calls the defense himself, an aggressive, man-coverage-friendly approach from his Lions coordinator days.

BAL.off_scheme: First-time and youngest play caller in the league; moving Lamar Jackson under center far more after years in the pistol, with an emphasis on detail and movement throws.
BAL.off_tree: Ben Johnson (Bears) and Sean Payton (Broncos, Saints)
BAL.def_scheme: Head coach Jesse Minter calls the defense, from the Harbaugh and Macdonald school of disguised coverages and simulated pressures.

CIN.off_scheme: The most pass-heavy offense in football over the past four years (67% designed passes), now hunting more explosive plays with Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
CIN.off_philosophy: Has kept play-calling duties through all eight seasons as head coach.

CLE.off_scheme: Architect of Baltimore's explosive offense (highest designed rush rate in the NFL, 2023-25) and Georgia's national-title offenses.
CLE.off_philosophy: Known for bending his scheme to fit his players; first-time NFL head coach with a young roster.

PIT.off_scheme: West Coast offense adapted for Aaron Rodgers: quick throws, timing routes and a heavy dose of slants.
PIT.off_philosophy: Long-time play caller who has occasionally handed off the duties and taken them back.

HOU.off_scheme: Spread-leaning personnel: three or more receivers on 70% of plays in 2025, the highest rate in the NFL.
HOU.off_tree: Josh McDaniels and Bill Belichick (Patriots), Sean McVay (Rams)
HOU.def_scheme: After an 0-4 start, Ryans took over defensive play calling from coordinator Matt Burke. A former 49ers defensive coordinator, he builds around a fast, attacking four-man rush.
HOU.change: Play-calling change after an 0-4 start: DeMeco Ryans now calls the defense.

IND.off_scheme: Play-action heavy (second-highest rate since 2023) with yards per play rising every year of his tenure.
IND.off_philosophy: Former Chargers and Eagles play caller; the 2025 offense was his most efficient in Indy until the quarterback injury.
IND.def_scheme: Multiple, disguise-heavy coverage looks from his Bengals years.

JAX.off_scheme: 11-personnel offense (three receivers) built for explosive plays; finished 2025 leading the NFL in scoring over an 8-0 closing stretch.
JAX.off_philosophy: Helped Baker Mayfield and then Trevor Lawrence to career years in back-to-back seasons.

TEN.off_scheme: Three-receiver base offense focused on developing Cam Ward in situational football: two-minute, red zone and third down.
TEN.off_tree: Bill Belichick (Patriots); former Bills coordinator and Giants head coach
TEN.def_scheme: Head coach Robert Saleh calls the defense: Seattle-tree 4-3 built on a fast, attacking front four.

DEN.off_scheme: Sean Payton's playbook with Webb's tweaks; Bo Nix moves out of the pocket often, and the focus is tempo, the run game and downfield accuracy.
DEN.off_philosophy: Webb opened 2026 as the play caller after Payton handed over the duties, but before Week 5 Payton took back a larger share of the offensive calls.
DEN.def_scheme: One of the league's most respected defensive play callers, with an aggressive, pressure-oriented approach.
DEN.change: Play-calling change before Week 5: Sean Payton is calling more of the offense again.

KC.off_scheme: West Coast system that threw the most screens in the NFL in 2025; this year shifting to more under-center snaps and play-action off the run game.
KC.off_tree: Andy Reid is the tree: Nagy, Pederson, Bieniemy and others came from his staffs
KC.off_philosophy: 28th straight season as his team's play caller, the longest active streak.

LV.off_scheme: Wide-zone West Coast offense with heavy personnel (12 and 21), bootlegs and outside runs that stretch defenses sideways; won a Super Bowl as Seattle's coordinator in 2025.

LAC.off_scheme: Motion, play-action and runs outside the tackles: in Miami his offenses ranked first in play-action rate and outside runs and near the top in motion and screens.

DAL.off_scheme: Up-tempo offense with lots of shifts and motion; second-fastest pace in the NFL since 2024.
DAL.off_philosophy: Veteran play caller (Jets, Rams, Seahawks) whose first year calling plays in Dallas produced nearly 30 points per game.

NYG.off_scheme: Andy Reid-style West Coast concepts and screens, mixed with Greg Roman's run game and tailored to Jaxson Dart.

PHI.off_scheme: Brand-new system: heavy play-action, more under center and throws over the middle, elements Philadelphia rarely used with Jalen Hurts.
PHI.off_tree: Influenced by Sean McVay, Kyle Shanahan and Matt LaFleur (Packers quarterbacks coach)
PHI.off_philosophy: First-time play caller and a former NFL quarterback.
PHI.def_scheme: Split-safety (two-high) coverage that disguises late and keeps everything in front, a structure much of the league has copied.
PHI.def_tree: Vic Fangio is the tree: Staley, Evero and others come from it

WAS.off_scheme: Moving to a play-action, under-center offense with far less no-huddle, while keeping some run-pass options from the previous system.
WAS.off_philosophy: First-time coordinator and play caller; expect some trick plays in the Ben Johnson mold.

CHI.off_scheme: Under center often, play-action on nearly a third of dropbacks (second in the NFL) and plenty of motion; one of few head coaches who installs his own run game.
CHI.off_philosophy: Fifth season calling plays after building Detroit's top offenses as coordinator.

DET.off_scheme: Physical and multiple, with personnel and focus changing week to week rather than running through one player.
DET.off_philosophy: First year in Detroit after three seasons as Arizona's coordinator.

GB.off_scheme: Run-leaning (fourth-highest designed rush rate in 2025) and rebuilding the offense from scratch after protection problems last season.

MIN.off_scheme: Under center more than most (third-lowest shotgun rate since 2022), with plays sequenced to set up big shots later in games.
MIN.off_philosophy: Historically pass-happy on short yardage, but called more designed runs in 2025.
MIN.def_scheme: Aggressive pressure packages and constantly changing looks to keep quarterbacks uncomfortable.

ATL.off_scheme: More under center and play-action, and a switch toward a gap-scheme run game; tight ends were heavily involved in his Cleveland offense.
ATL.off_philosophy: Followed Kevin Stefanski from Cleveland; previously called plays at Notre Dame and Alabama.

CAR.off_scheme: First-time play caller running Dave Canales' offense, which led the NFL in fourth-down conversions in 2025.
CAR.off_philosophy: Head coach Dave Canales handed over the play sheet this offseason; veteran play caller Darrell Bevell is on staff as associate head coach.

NO.off_scheme: Shotgun-heavy and motion-heavy: no team ran more plays combining the two in 2025.
NO.off_philosophy: Has called plays since his Cowboys coordinator days; first full season with Tyler Shough as the starter.

TB.off_scheme: Run-leaning (Atlanta had the fifth-highest designed rush rate under him in 2025), roughly half carryover and half new compared with last year.
TB.def_scheme: Bowles calls the defense himself and has no separate coordinator: blitz-heavy and aggressive.

ARI.off_scheme: Motion-heavy (the Rams led the NFL in motion at the snap while he was coordinator), with one of the league's best skill groups.
ARI.off_philosophy: First-year head coach; last called plays regularly as the Jets' coordinator in 2021-22.

LA.off_scheme: Play-action heavy; injuries in 2025 pushed him into more three-tight-end (13 personnel) plays than any team in nearly two decades.
LA.off_tree: Sean McVay is the tree: Zac Taylor, Kevin O'Connell, Liam Coen, Zac Robinson and others

SF.off_scheme: Wide-zone run game, lots of pre-snap motion and under-center play-action (third-highest under-center rate since 2017).
SF.off_tree: Kyle Shanahan is the tree: LaFleur, McDaniel, Kubiak and others

SEA.off_scheme: West Coast offense close to Klint Kubiak's 2025 Super Bowl attack, adding more pre-snap motion and two-back sets; the most run-heavy offense in 2025 by designed rush rate.
SEA.off_philosophy: First-time coordinator chosen so the scheme wouldn't have to start over.
SEA.def_scheme: Head coach Mike Macdonald calls the defense: disguised coverages and simulated pressures that make quarterbacks guess.
